name: manual_983388
claim: An async fallback that duplicates a sync helper's logic in a separate implementation (e.g. its own httpx.AsyncClient instead of asyncio.to_thread wrapping the sync helper) is a real drift risk, not just a style nitpick -- the two paths can silently diverge on the exact same decision (e.g. SSRF local/remote classification) for the same input

decisions.notes: orchestrator/orama_bridge.py's async HTTP fallback had its own httpx.AsyncClient call for local endpoints, separate from the sync call_oramasys_bridge()'s httpx.post call -- both implementing the identical local/remote classification independently. GitHub issue #361 named this exact risk. Fixed by extracting one _dispatch_oramasys_http() function; sync calls it directly, async wraps it in asyncio.to_thread(). Verified via inspect.getsource() assertion that both code paths route through the same function object, not just equivalent-looking code. General rule: when a sync/async pair need identical branching logic, write it once and have async wrap the sync version via to_thread -- never hand-write the same decision twice.
